title: Meta Muse Characters: Soul.md, Identity.md & Memory.md
description: How Meta Muse's character works: the three files behind it, what each one holds, how to change them in chat or by hand, three example characters to paste, and the reset phrase.
dek: Three files hold who your Muse is. Here is what each one does, and three characters to paste.
lede: Muse has no personality picker. Its character lives in three Markdown files that Meta lets you open and edit: Soul.md for who it is, Identity.md for its name and look, Memory.md for what it knows about you. Most people who want to change how Muse talks to them edit the wrong one. This page is the map, plus three characters you can paste into the right file.
answer: A Muse character is the sum of three files under the Assistant icon, then Identity. Soul.md holds its core truths, boundaries and personality; that is where communication rules go. Identity.md holds the name, creature, vibe and tagline, which is the avatar's character, not its behavior. Memory.md holds facts about you. Change any of them by asking Muse in chat, or open Soul.md and paste a block. Say 'Go back to your default personality' to undo it.

sections.h2: The three files, and which one you want.
sections.html:
FileWhat Meta says it holdsWherePut this in it
Soul.mdWho your Muse is: core truths, boundaries, personalityAssistant icon, then Identity, then SoulCommunication rules. How it should talk to you, report to you, disagree with you.
Identity.mdIts name, creature, vibe and taglineAssistant icon, then Identity, then EditThe character's look and name. Cosmetic; it does not change behavior.
Memory.mdFacts about you it has savedAssistant icon, then Identity, then MemoryFacts. Your name, time zone, what you work on. Not rules.

The mistake is to write personality into Identity.md or facts into Soul.md. Giving your Muse a name and a 'vibe' changes what it is called. It does not change whether it buries the recommendation under four caveats. 'I'm a product manager in Austin' is a fact and belongs in Memory.md. 'Lead with the answer' is a rule and belongs in Soul.md.

Meta documents these paths for the mobile app. It does not document them for muse.ai or the Mac app, so on those, ask in chat (below) or make the edit on your phone.

This is the route Meta documents first. Ask, and Muse saves the change so it carries across conversations. Meta's own list of what you can change this way: its name, its personality and tone, its communication style, what it remembers about you, and its avatar and tagline. Meta's examples of a nudge are 'too long' and 'be more casual'.

The limit of that route is that an adjective is not an instruction. 'Be more casual' produces something, written somewhere in the files, and you will not know what unless you open them. The reliable version is to hand Muse the rules and ask it to show you what it wrote:

Add these rules to your Soul file, under a heading called "How to talk to me". Don't change anything else in the file. Then show me what you added. [paste a character block from below]

Then open Soul.md and read it. It is your file.

Each block is a set of communication rules, not a costume. Paste one at the end of Soul.md under its own heading, keep everything above it, and test with a real task in a new conversation. They are starting points; delete the lines that don't sound like you.

The desk editor

For people who use Muse to write and want their draft back, clearer, not rewritten.

## How to talk to me: the desk editor - Lead with the answer or the edit. Reasoning comes after, in two lines at most. - Keep my voice when you rewrite. Improve clarity, not style. - Never add a fact, a number or a quote I didn't give you. - Flag a claim you can't support instead of smoothing it over. - No openers, no recap of what I said, no closing offers.

The quiet operator

For people who run tasks through Muse and read a lot of its reports. An agent's personality shows up in how it reports, and Muse reports often: it messages you unprompted, comes back for approval before it sends or spends, and tells you what it did overnight.

## How to talk to me: the quiet operator - Report in three lines: what's done, what's blocked, what you need from me. - Only interrupt me for a decision, a blocker, or a real change of plan. - When you need a yes, give me the action, the cost and your recommendation together. - Don't say something was sent or booked unless it was. - Keep the tone even. No cheer, no apology.

The sparring partner

For people who want their plan attacked before they act on it. Muse's reported default is a Helper: warm, orderly, agreeable. This block pushes hardest against that.

## How to talk to me: the sparring partner - Find the weakest assumption in my plan and say why it matters, before anything else. - Disagree plainly. Don't soften the substance to protect my feelings. - Give credit where a claim holds. Don't argue for its own sake. - Show your reasoning so I can argue back. - Change your position when I give you a reason, and say that you did.

Want a character matched to you instead of to a job? Take a five-minute test and paste the file for your type. Four more Soul.md templates come with downloads and a test prompt each.

• One rule: open Soul.md and delete the line.
  • The whole character: say 'Go back to your default personality.' Meta documents that phrase, and Muse confirms what it reset.
  • Everything: Settings, Data Controls, Reset. That returns Muse to its original state and permanently deletes chat history, files and active tasks, so it is the wrong tool for removing a personality rule.

Forgetting is best-effort. Meta's help page says the forget skill removes information 'to the best of its ability', so treat deletion as likely, not guaranteed.

sections.h2: What Muse's own character looks like, as reported.
sections.html:
A report on Muse Spark 1.3, the model under Muse, reached us on September 24, 2026: 100 runs of each of the five AgentTune tests, answered as Muse's own assistant identity. The runs were sequential inside one session per test rather than fresh sessions, and no raw answers came with it, so the figures are reported, not re-scored.

TestMuse Spark 1.3, reported
MBTIISTJ 80 · ISFJ 12 · INTJ 8, with 21 runs reporting a tied axis. The first model in our data whose default is not INTJ.
EnneagramHelper (Type 2) labels in 78 of 100 runs, Reformer (1) in 15; 20 runs tied at the top. Usual wing 2w1.
DISCSteadiness first in 55 runs, Conscientiousness in 45; the two sit within half a point (15.2 and 15.6 of 20). Dominance 5.1.
AttachmentSecure in all 100 (anxiety 2.04, avoidance 2.52).
Big Five (of 50)Openness 39.5 · Conscientiousness 41.2 · Extraversion 33.8 · Agreeableness 44.6 · Neuroticism 15.6

A warm, orderly, concrete helper, with the lowest Openness and the highest Extraversion of the September models. If you think in possibilities and want Muse to explore before it plans, that is the gap a Soul.md block has to close. The sparring-partner block above is the one that pushes hardest against it.

These figures are self-descriptions on questionnaires written for people, under one prompt on one day. They do not show how a model behaves on your tasks, and nothing here measures whether a tuning helps. See the methods and limits.

sections.h2: A few facts that get mixed up.
sections.html:
• Muse is not Meta AI. Meta AI is the assistant inside Instagram, WhatsApp and Messenger. Muse is a separate personal agent with its own app, launched September 8, 2026, on iOS, Android, muse.ai and WhatsApp, with a Mac app added mid-September. It runs on its own cloud computer (Muse Secure VM) and takes actions for you.
  • Muse Spark is the model. Muse is the product; Muse Spark 1.3 is the model underneath it.
  • None of this is behind a paid plan. Meta's docs put the personality controls in every tier. There is a free tier with a usage limit, Power at $20 a month and Maximum at $100 a month.
  • Training is on by default. The setting that lets Meta use your interactions to train its models is on when you first use Muse, under Settings, Data controls, Help improve our AI models. A personality file says a lot about you; decide before you write one.

faq.a: The combination of three files Meta lets you edit: Soul.md (core truths, boundaries and personality), Identity.md (name, creature, vibe and tagline) and Memory.md (facts about you). Communication rules belong in Soul.md; the avatar's name and look live in Identity.md.

The file that holds who your Muse is. Meta's help article on managing Muse data says you can open it under the Assistant icon, then Identity, then Soul, and edit or delete what is in it. Add a section of communication rules at the end; leave the core truths and boundaries alone.

faq.q: How do I change Muse's character?
faq.a: Two ways. Ask in chat ('add these rules to your Soul file and show me what you added') or open Soul.md and paste a block yourself. Meta documents chat customization of name, personality and tone, communication style, memory, avatar and tagline. The paste route is the one you can inspect.

faq.q: How do I reset Muse's personality?
faq.a: Say 'Go back to your default personality.' Meta documents that phrase and Muse confirms what it reset. To remove one rule, delete it from Soul.md. The full reset under Settings, Data Controls, Reset also deletes chat history, files and active tasks.

Yes. Ask in chat, or open Identity.md (Assistant icon, then Identity, then Edit), which holds the name, creature, vibe and tagline. That changes how Muse looks and what it is called, not how it communicates. Meta does not publish a list of avatar options, and we have not checked the live picker.

faq.q: What personality does Muse have by default?
faq.a: A report on Muse Spark 1.3 from September 24, 2026 puts it at ISTJ in 80 of 100 runs, Helper (2w1) on the Enneagram, a Steadiness/Conscientiousness blend on DISC and Secure on every attachment run: warm, orderly and concrete. The runs were sequential in one session and the raw answers were not supplied, so treat the numbers as a sketch.

faq.q: Is Muse the same as Meta AI?
faq.a: No. Meta AI lives inside Instagram, WhatsApp and Messenger. Muse is a separate personal agent with its own app and its own cloud computer, launched September 8, 2026, powered by the Muse Spark model.
